Indirect discrimination

9. The full definition of indirect discrimination is set out in the EqA 2010 overview above.
Subject to the defence of justification, it is indirect age discrimination to apply a PCP which
puts someone of a certain age group at a particular disadvantage, and which puts, or would
put, others of the same group at that disadvantage.
For example, an optician allows payment for glasses by instalments, but restricts eligibility to
those in work. The optician’s practice applies to everyone but puts people over retirement
age at a disadvantage. This is unlawful discrimination unless the practice is justified.
